Spatial frequency (ν=1/Λ)

Words: 39
Fourier analysis OurBigBook.com
Spatial frequency is the number of oscillation cycles per unit length. A ripple with spatial period Λ has frequency ν=1/Λ; its angular wavenumber is k=2πν. In two dimensions the spatial-frequency vector specifies the orientation and period of a plane-wave pattern.

Nyquist–Shannon sampling theorem

Words: 225 Articles: 3
Fourier analysis OurBigBook.com
A suitably band-limited function can be reconstructed from equally spaced samples when the sampling rate exceeds twice its largest ordinary frequency. Sampling more slowly aliases distinct frequencies in the Fourier transform. For spatial sampling, the same statement relates sample pitch to the shortest resolvable wavelength.

Strictly supercritical sampling alias counterexample (g(t)=sin(πt)h(t),g(n)=0)

Words: 67
Nyquist–Shannon sampling theorem OurBigBook.com
For every ϵ>0, choose a nonzero smooth spectral bump supported in (−ϵ0​,ϵ0​) with ϵ0​<min(ϵ,π), and let h be its inverse Fourier transform. Then g is a nonzero Schwartz function, vanishes on all integer samples, and its transform is the difference of bumps shifted to π and −π. Its support lies strictly within [−π−ϵ,π+ϵ]. Thus even a small bandwidth increase destroys uniqueness from unit-spaced samples.

Sampling expansion by periodic Fourier projection (f(t)=∑n∈Z​f(n)sinc(t−n))

Words: 66
Nyquist–Shannon sampling theorem OurBigBook.com
When the continuous Fourier transform F of an integrable function vanishes outside [−π,π], its periodic Fourier coefficients are the integer samples of f, with the sign of the index reversed. Projecting F in L2[−π,π] and then applying the Fourier inversion theorem gives the displayed sinc function reconstruction. The Cauchy-Schwarz inequality controls the reconstruction error uniformly in t. Bessel's inequality bounds the shifted sinc coefficient vector, giving absolute uniform tails when the sample sequence belongs to ℓ2.

Nyquist spatial frequency (νmax​=1/(2p))

Words: 49
Nyquist–Shannon sampling theorem OurBigBook.com
Samples spaced by pitch p can distinguish spatial frequencies strictly below 1/(2p) cycles per unit length. Thus the shortest limiting wavelength is 2p; exactly at the limit a sinusoid's phase can make all samples vanish. A practical deformable mirror has additional limits from actuator influence functions and finite pupil geometry.

Euclidean lattice

Words: 718 Articles: 12
Fourier analysis OurBigBook.com
A Euclidean lattice is a discrete subgroup Λ⊆Rn spanning the ambient vector space. Its covolume m(Λ) is the volume of a fundamental parallelepiped.

Lenstra-Lenstra-Lovász lattice basis reduction algorithm (δ=3/4,∣μij​∣≤1/2)

Words: 104
Euclidean lattice OurBigBook.com
For an integer basis of a Euclidean lattice, the algorithm uses integer column operations and swaps to obtain a size-reduced basis with Gram-Schmidt coefficients ∣μij​∣≤1/2 and the condition δ∥bi∗​∥2≤∥bi+1∗​∥2+μi+1,i2​∥bi∗​∥2. It preserves the lattice and exposes short vectors and near-relations. It is useful for improving proven Diophantine bounds by encoding scaled logarithms in integer coordinates. A certified lower bound for every nonzero lattice vector is mini​∥bi∗​∥: in a nonzero integer linear combination, project onto the last nonzero Gram-Schmidt direction. Better-reduced bases improve this lower bound. Rounding and logarithm errors must still be bounded before turning it into a certified lower bound for a logarithmic form.

Complex lattice (Λ=Zω1​+Zω2​⊂C)

Words: 81 Articles: 1
Euclidean lattice OurBigBook.com
A complex lattice is a discrete rank-two subgroup of the complex plane, generated by two real-linearly independent periods. An oriented basis can be chosen with Im(ω1​/ω2​)>0. Scaling by ω2−1​ then gives Zτ+Z for a point in the complex upper half-plane.

Homothety of complex lattices (Λ′=aΛ, a∈C×)

Words: 40
Complex lattice OurBigBook.com
Two complex lattices are homothetic when multiplication by one nonzero complex number takes one onto the other. Changes between oriented integral bases have determinant one, so normalized period ratios classify these classes by SL2​(Z)\H. The lattice Eisenstein sums scale as Gk​(aΛ)=a−kGk​(Λ).

Tetracode length-isospectral lattice construction (L±​=(±3I+S)Z4)

Words: 293 Articles: 3
Euclidean lattice OurBigBook.com
For the skew matrix S=(0−1−1−1​101−1​1−101​11−10​), both Euclidean lattices reduce to the tetracode modulo 3. A reflection depending on the reduction coset matches their vectors coordinatewise in absolute value. Their weighted length spectra agree for all positive diagonal axis weights. Rationally independent weights force any possible linear isometry to be a coordinate sign change; the code then forces an overall sign, which does not identify the two lattices.

Rationally independent axis weights obstruct a lattice isometry (∑i​ai​xi2​=∑i​ai​yi2​⟹xi2​=yi2​)

Words: 95
Tetracode length-isospectral lattice construction OurBigBook.com
Choose positive axis weights linearly independent over the rationals, and suppose both integer Euclidean lattices contain qZd for some positive integer q. A length-preserving linear map sends each qei​ to an integer vector with exactly that absolute-coordinate pattern, by the displayed implication. Thus the map must be a diagonal sign change. For the four-coordinate tetracode, preserving the code forces all four signs to agree, because each of its four nonzero projective words has support on a different triple of coordinates. A global sign cannot exchange the two odd-vector parity conditions, proving nonisometry for these weights.

Parity congruence description of tetracode lattices (xmod3∈T,x1​≡⋯≡x4​(mod2))

Words: 67
Tetracode length-isospectral lattice construction OurBigBook.com
Add respectively the conditions ∑i​xi​≡0(mod4) and ∑i​xi​−2x1​≡0(mod4) to the displayed common conditions. These define the two integer Euclidean lattices underlying the tetracode length-isospectral lattice construction. They coincide on their all-even vectors and differ on all-odd vectors. Reflecting a coordinate divisible by three preserves the code condition; on odd vectors it changes the coordinate sum by two modulo four, while on even vectors both conditions remain satisfied. This yields the coordinate reflection bijection for tetracode lattices.

Coordinate reflection bijection for tetracode lattices (v↦v−2vi​ei​)

Words: 69
Tetracode length-isospectral lattice construction OurBigBook.com
For the tetracode length-isospectral lattice construction L±​=(±3I+S)Z4, choose the first coordinate i divisible by three and reverse its sign. Such a coordinate always exists because each nonzero tetracode word has one zero coordinate. The reflection preserves the reduction modulo three and switches the two lattice membership conditions modulo four. It is an involution between L+​ and L−​ preserving every absolute coordinate, so arbitrary positive diagonal weights preserve equality of their vector-length multisets.

Covolume (covol(Λ))

Words: 43
Euclidean lattice OurBigBook.com
The covolume of a full Euclidean lattice is the Lebesgue measure of a fundamental parallelepiped in its ambient inner product space. In orthonormal coordinates it is ∣detB∣ for a lattice basis matrix B. Scaling the lattice by t>0 multiplies the covolume by tn; the dual lattice has reciprocal covolume.

Shortest-independent-vector basis lemma

Words: 64
Euclidean lattice OurBigBook.com
In a rank-two Euclidean lattice, a shortest nonzero vector v and a shortest vector w∈/Zv form a basis. The shortest vector is primitive. If the vertical coordinate of w has index m≥2 in the projection lattice, a vector with smaller positive vertical coordinate can be reduced horizontally to length squared at most (∣v∣2+∣w∣2)/4<∣w∣2, a contradiction. This lemma need not hold in higher rank.

Lattice-point asymptotics by fundamental cells (N(R)=vol(B1​)Rd/A+O(Rd−1))

Words: 48
Euclidean lattice OurBigBook.com
For a full-rank Euclidean lattice of covolume A in Rd, bounded fundamental cells compare lattice points in a radius-R ball with the volumes of balls of radii R±C. Hence N(R)=vol(B1​)Rd/A+O(Rd−1). A lattice norm multiset therefore determines the covolume, which is useful for the spectrum of a flat torus.

Characters of a real torus (Λ∨≅Homcts​(Rn/Λ,C×))

Words: 45
Dual lattice OurBigBook.com
Every continuous group homomorphism Rn/Λ→C× is x+Λ↦e2πi⟨u,x⟩ for a unique u in the dual lattice. Compactness forces unit modulus, and lifting the character to the simply connected cover makes its phase a real linear functional. These characters are the frequencies of torus Fourier series.

Fourier analysis OurBigBook.com
For a sufficiently rapidly decreasing function f, the Poisson summation formula relates its samples to those of its Fourier transform:
∑n∈Z​f(n)=∑k∈Z​f​(2πk)
(2)
under the convention f​(ξ)=∫R​f(x)e−ixξdx.

Periodization of an integrable function (g(t)=∑k∈Z​F(t+2πk))

Words: 107
Poisson summation formula OurBigBook.com
For F∈L1(R) the periodization is absolutely convergent almost everywhere in a period by integrating the sum of absolute values. Its Fourier series coefficient is cn​=F(n)/(2π), where F(ω)=∫R​F(x)e−iωxdx. Absolute integrability permits integrating term by term and changing variables across the disjoint period intervals. This coefficient identity does not by itself assert pointwise convergence of the ordinary Fourier series. Even uniform convergence of the original periodization cannot repair arbitrary point values: F=1{0}​ has zero transform and a nonzero periodization at multiples of 2π. Additional regularity, such as a continuous piecewise continuously differentiable periodization, validates the pointwise Poisson summation formula in this setting.

Periodization of a Schwartz function (Pf​(x)=∑n∈Z​f(x+n))

Words: 64
Poisson summation formula OurBigBook.com
For a Schwartz function on the real numbers, its periodization is a smooth periodic function of period one. Rapid decay gives uniform convergence on [0,1] of the series and each differentiated series. Under the Fourier transform convention f​(ξ)=∫f(x)e−2πixξdx, its mth Fourier coefficient is f​(m): integrate termwise over one period and combine the translated intervals. The rapidly decreasing coefficients give a Fourier series with uniform convergence. Evaluation at zero proves the Poisson summation formula.

Wavelet

Words: 2k Articles: 39
Fourier analysis OurBigBook.com
A wavelet is a localized function whose translates and dilates analyze different positions and scales.

Discrete wavelet transform ((a,b)=((u+v)/2​,(u−v)/2​))

Words: 85
Wavelet OurBigBook.com
A discrete wavelet transform computes multiscale approximation and detail coefficients from sampled data. In the Haar wavelet construction, apply the displayed orthogonal sum/difference transformation to each adjacent pair and repeat on the approximation coefficients. The detail coefficients at each stage and the last approximation coefficient preserve the squared Euclidean norm, because the two-by-two transform is orthogonal. For dyadic sample size, multiplying the resulting coefficients by n−1/2 gives the normalized coefficients of the wavelet regression estimator on [0,1]. Under independent Gaussian noise, orthogonality preserves the common coefficient noise variance and independence.

Wavelet series (m=∑k​a0,k​ϕ0,k​+∑j≥0,k​bj,k​ψj,k​)

Words: 54
Wavelet OurBigBook.com
For an orthonormal wavelet and its scaling function, set ϕj,k​(x)=2j/2ϕ(2jx−k) and similarly for ψ. The coarse scaling functions together with nonnegative-resolution wavelets form an orthonormal basis of L2(R). The coefficients are the corresponding L2 inner products. The series converges in the L2 norm, and the Parseval identity for a Hilbertian basis equates squared norm with the sum of squared coefficients. Pointwise convergence requires additional hypotheses.

Tensor-product wavelet basis

Words: 149 Articles: 2
Wavelet OurBigBook.com
From a one-dimensional multiresolution analysis, the simultaneous-scale two-dimensional detail space splits as (Wj​⊗Vj​)⊕(Vj​⊗Wj​)⊕(Wj​⊗Wj​). Its generating wavelets are ψ⊗φ, φ⊗ψ, and ψ⊗ψ. Their normalized dilates are 2jΨ(2j⋅−k) for k∈Z2. Include a coarse scaling family when working on a bounded square.

Wavelet approximation across a curve

Words: 65
Tensor-product wavelet basis OurBigBook.com
A finite-length smooth curve meets O(2j) supports of localized two-dimensional wavelets at scale j. For a bounded function, their coefficients are O(2−j), so their total squared energy at that scale is O(2−j). Keeping these coefficients through level J uses O(2J) terms and leaves squared error O(2−J). Polynomial cancellation, or adequate approximation of the remaining smooth regions, therefore gives best N-term approximation squared error O(N−1).

Tensor-product wavelet

Words: 38
Tensor-product wavelet basis OurBigBook.com
A tensor-product wavelet is a product of one-dimensional wavelets and scaling functions, with at least one wavelet factor. In two dimensions, the three simultaneous-scale types are ψ⊗φ, φ⊗ψ and ψ⊗ψ. Their translates and normalized dilates form a tensor-product wavelet basis.

Interval-adapted wavelet basis

Words: 146 Articles: 2
Wavelet OurBigBook.com
An interval-adapted wavelet basis is an orthonormal basis of L2[0,1] made of a finite coarse scaling function family and resolution-indexed wavelets. A localized construction modifies only a bounded number of functions near each endpoint at every level. Boundary modification must preserve nested refinement spaces and the required vanishing moments; simple restriction of a whole-line basis does not do so.

Boundary wavelet

Words: 92 Articles: 1
Interval-adapted wavelet basis OurBigBook.com
A boundary wavelet replaces a translated interior wavelet whose support of a function meets a domain endpoint. Compatible finite boundary refinement matrices preserve orthogonality and localization across scales. If the coarse boundary spaces reproduce polynomials of degree less than q, their detail-space orthogonal complements have q vanishing moments.
Cohen-Daubechies-Vial interval wavelet construction
Words: 52
Boundary wavelet OurBigBook.com
This construction adapts compactly supported orthonormal wavelets to an interval by finite changes near its endpoints. It preserves local support, polynomial reproduction, nested approximation spaces and orthogonal detail spaces. The resulting basis contains coarse scaling functions, unchanged interior wavelets, and finitely many boundary wavelets per endpoint and per scale, without forcing periodic or zero boundary values.

Vanishing moment (∫xrψ(x)dx=0)

Words: 163 Articles: 2
Wavelet OurBigBook.com
A wavelet has q vanishing moments when these integrals vanish for 0≤r<q. For compact support, this is equivalent to a zero of order at least q at the origin of its Fourier transform. Such a wavelet annihilates polynomials of degree less than q, and a Taylor polynomial bounds coefficients on smooth regions.

Smooth-mask vanishing-moment criterion

Words: 115 Articles: 1
Vanishing moment OurBigBook.com
Suppose an integrable orthonormal scaling function has a low-pass filter of a multiresolution analysis that is Cp−1 near π, and its Fourier transform is Cp−1 near zero. If the associated wavelet has p integrable vanishing moments, then m(k)(π)=0 for k<p. Indeed, moment differentiation of the Fourier transform makes ψ​(k)(0)=0, while ∣φ​(0)∣=1. In ψ​(2t)=e−itm(t+π)​φ​(t), division by the nonzero smooth factor proves the conclusion. With only continuity of that factor one still obtains a Peano zero, but not automatically higher ordinary derivatives.
Integer-frequency zeros of a scaling function
Words: 52
Smooth-mask vanishing-moment criterion OurBigBook.com
Assume the scaling function Fourier transform and the MRA low-pass filter are Cp−1, and m(k)(π)=0 for k<p. For every nonzero integer j, write j=2rℓ with ℓ odd. Iterating the scaling refinement equation at 2πj+t supplies a factor m(πℓ+t/2r+1). All its derivatives of order less than p vanish at t=0, by periodicity. The product rule gives φ​(k)(2πj)=0 for k<p.

Orthonormal wavelet

Words: 646 Articles: 11
Wavelet OurBigBook.com
An orthonormal wavelet ψ generates {2j/2ψ(2jx−k)}j,k∈Z​ as an orthonormal basis of L2(R).

Daubechies wavelet

Words: 61
Orthonormal wavelet OurBigBook.com
A Daubechies wavelet of order q is a compact support orthonormal wavelet with q vanishing moments and a minimal-length finite refinement filter. The minimal filter has 2q taps, giving support length 2q−1 in the standard dyadic normalization. Its low-pass symbol has a zero of order q at π. Increasing order improves polynomial cancellation and, for sufficiently large order, regularity, at the price of a wider support.

Haar wavelet (ψ=χ[0,1/2)​−χ[1/2,1)​)

Words: 570 Articles: 9
Orthonormal wavelet OurBigBook.com
The Haar wavelet has one vanishing moment and compact support of unit length. Its scaling function is χ[0,1)​, and its refinement coefficients are h0​=h1​=1/2​. The approximation spaces consist of functions constant on dyadic cells. Its discontinuity makes it effective for jump localization but limits smooth-function approximation.
Uniform hard-threshold convergence of normalized Haar expansions (∥∑∣cH​∣≥δ​cH​H−f∥∞​→0)
Words: 165 Articles: 1
Haar wavelet OurBigBook.com
Use the full orthonormal Haar system, including the constant function. Dyadic partial sums are cell averages and converge uniformly for continuous f. On a cell of length ℓ, a normalized detail has ∣cH​∣≤ωf​(ℓ)ℓ​ and pointwise size ∣H∣=ℓ−1/2. Fix a coarse level where the modulus is small. Above a level chosen by δ/ℓ​ reaching that small modulus, no detail can survive the threshold. Below it, omitted details along any one dyadic chain sum to a geometric bound. Thus the thresholded expansion differs from a sufficiently fine cell average by a uniformly small amount.
Geometric bound for omitted Haar details (∑j=JK​δ/L2−j​≤1−2−1/2δ2K/2/L​​)
Words: 70
Uniform hard-threshold convergence of normalized Haar expansions OurBigBook.com
At each point there is at most one supported Haar wavelet per scale. If a detail coefficient is below δ, its value there is at most δ2j/2/L​. Summing these bounds up to level K gives the displayed geometric estimate. Selecting K so the final term is of the order of the modulus of continuity controls all omitted fine details, even though arbitrary deletions from a uniformly convergent series need not preserve convergence.
Haar refinement identity (Vj+1​=Vj​⊕Wj​)
Words: 53
